body.en: Because resources are scarce, every economy must decide: what to produce and in what quantities; how to produce, that is, with labour-intensive or capital-intensive techniques; and for whom to produce, that is, how output is distributed. Two more *problems* are the full and efficient use of resources and the growth of resources over time.

points.en: What to produce: allocation of resources
How to produce: choice of technique
For whom to produce: distribution of income
Full employment and growth of resources

On the board: A PPC schedule.

body.en: A *production possibility curve* (PPC) shows the combinations of two goods an economy can produce with given resources and technology, when the resources are fully and efficiently used. It slopes down because more of one good means less of the other. It is concave to the origin because resources are not equally suited to both goods, so the marginal opportunity cost (MOC) of a good rises as more of it is made. A point inside shows idle resources; a point outside is unattainable; growth shifts the curve outward.

points.en: Slopes downward: scarcity forces a trade-off
Outward shift: more resources or better technology

problem.en: Using the schedule on the board, find the opportunity cost of moving from point C (2 cloth, 12 wheat) to point E (4 cloth, 5 wheat). Explain why the PPC is concave.

steps.en: Cloth rises by 2 units; wheat falls from 12 to 5, that is by 7 units.
Average opportunity cost = 7/2 = 3.5 units of wheat per unit of cloth.
Unit by unit the MOC is 3 then 4: it rises because resources suited to wheat are shifted to cloth.

answer.en: 7 units of wheat for 2 units of cloth; the MOC rises, so the PPC is concave.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Using the schedule on the board, find the opportunity cost of moving from point C (2 cloth, 12 wheat) to point E (4 cloth, 5 wheat). Explain why the PPC is concave.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Using the schedule on the board, find the opportunity cost of moving from point C (2 cloth, 12 wheat) to point E (4 cloth, 5 wheat). Explain why the PPC is concave.
Cloth rises by 2 units; wheat falls from 12 to 5, that is by 7 units.
Average opportunity cost equals 7 over 2 equals 3.5 units of wheat per unit of cloth.
Unit by unit the MOC is 3 then 4: it rises because resources suited to wheat are shifted to cloth.
So the answer is 7 units of wheat for 2 units of cloth; the MOC rises, so the PPC is concave.
